section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a study (referred to as Study X) that investigated how a woman's self-compassion influences her eating, body image, and affect when interacting with body-focused others. The study involved 92 female undergraduates who reported daily on these variables for seven nights. Results indicated that self-compassion buffered the negative impact of interactions with body-focused others on body image concerns and negative affect, and positively influenced body appreciation and intuitive eating.
